headline: Ward 36 scores high on reputation, low on room per resident.
summary:
Ward 36's best numbers are about reputation. Its houses of worship carry one of the highest median Google ratings in Chicago, fourth of fifty wards, and its bars rate fifth among wards with enough of them to measure. Nine local congregations clear a 4.8 rating with at least 25 reviews, good for sixth place citywide. The ward's photo on this page is one of those churches, Saints Volodymyr and Olha. Worship is the strongest single thing this ward has going for it. Two more first-place finishes, most bills sponsored and the largest alley-repair share of menu money, belong to the alderman's office rather than to anyone who lives here.

The weak side of the ward's scorecard is mostly about room. Park acreage lands in the bottom five citywide, barely three acres per 10,000 residents, and mental health providers run just over two per 10,000, one of the thinnest counts in the city relative to population. Parking complaints land in the bottom five too, nearly 620 per square kilometer. Only one landmark in the ward is formally mapped, a strange count for a ward whose defining photo is a church, the same kind of building that helped earn Ward 36 some of the best worship ratings anywhere in Chicago. None of this eases up soon. The city approved a 40-unit building on the ward's Ukrainian Village edge this spring, adding residents to a ward that already runs thin on park space per person.
reading_the_rankings: Two of Ward 36's numbers read stronger than they are. Being first in the city for bills sponsored sounds like an unusually productive council seat. The count is of introductions rather than of anything passed or funded, the source rates the figure medium confidence, and it describes one officeholder rather than the blocks he represents. Fifth place for traffic proximity, meaning this ward supposedly sees less traffic exposure than all but four others in Chicago, is assigned by census tract rather than measured street by street, and fourteen other wards land within two points of this one, so a handful of ranks in either direction come down to noise.

news.headline: Ukrainian Village, Bucktown Apartment Proposals Approved By City Council
news.note: City Council approved a 40-unit apartment building at Chicago and Washtenaw avenues on the Ukrainian Village-Humboldt Park border, part of Ward 36, after two rounds of community meetings over the project's size.

news.headline: With Airbag Thefts Still Up, Could A New Ordinance Curb The Black Market Sales Fueling Them?
news.note: An ordinance backed by Ald. Gilbert Villegas targets auto shops that resell stolen airbags, responding to a rise in thefts across the Northwest Side, including parts of Ward 36.

news.headline: City Council committee backs crackdown on selling weed near schools, parks
news.note: A City Council committee advanced an ordinance from Ward 36's Ald. Gilbert Villegas penalizing marijuana sales near schools and parks, after a scaled back compromise on the restricted zone.
